title: PKGPT: Expert-Orchestrated Recursive LLM Agent for Automated NONMEM PopPK Modeling with Human Benchmarking

content.abstract_summary: PKGPT is a recursive, five-phase agentic LLM system (powered by Gemini 3.0 Flash) that automates NONMEM-based PopPK model development and benchmarks its performance against human expert models on three public datasets. The system iteratively executes NONMEM, parses outputs, and refines control streams across phases: base model, structural diagnostics, overfitting reduction, random-effects optimization, and covariate analysis. Naïve zero-shot LLM prompting consistently fails (non-executable code); the agentic loop produces executable, converging models but exhibits physiological plausibility failures and variable reproducibility.
key_findings: Naïve zero-shot LLM prompting typically produces NONMEM code that fails to execute — the agentic feedback loop is necessary for convergence
Warfarin: PKGPT and human both selected one-compartment oral (ADVAN2), but expert achieved OFV 294.41 vs PKGPT's 484.43 via covariate scaling
Theophylline: PKGPT produced parameter estimates close to expert (Ka=1.59 vs 1.46 h; CL=0.0399 vs 0.0404 L/h/kg)
Tobramycin: PKGPT correctly identified two-compartment structure but produced physiologically implausible V2=149 L vs expert's 13.2 L — a 11-fold plausibility error
PKGPT did not identify clinically established covariates across all three datasets — covariate analysis remains a critical gap
Run-to-run reproducibility was variable — consistent with shin_2024_llm but not resolved by the agentic architecture
Human-in-the-loop oversight remains essential for physiological plausibility and clinical interpretability despite successful numerical convergence
limitations: Only three standard PopPK datasets tested — all 1-cpt or 2-cpt; no PBPK, QSP, or stiff ODE systems
Single LLM backend (Gemini 3.0 Flash) — not a comparative study across models
Covariate identification failed across all datasets — the system's covariate analysis phase is weakest
Variable reproducibility not quantified — no formal reproducibility metric reported
No identifiability assessment of generated models
Physiological plausibility scoring was qualitative (V2 comparison), not systematized

extracted_claims.text: PKGPT consistently produced executable, converging NONMEM models across all three datasets.
In tobramycin, PKGPT correctly identified a two-compartment structure but produced physiologically implausible peripheral volume estimates (V2 = 149 L vs. expert's 13.2 L).
Across datasets, PKGPT did not identify clinically established covariates, and run-to-run reproducibility was variable.

PKGPT substantially improves the robustness and usability of LLM-generated NONMEM code compared with naïve zero-shot prompting, accelerating model drafting and iterative refinement, but physiological plausibility and clinical interpretability still require a human-in-the-loop oversight.

numerical_findings.description: OFV for warfarin one-compartment model: PKGPT vs. human expert
Theophylline Ka estimate: PKGPT vs. human expert
Tobramycin V2 estimate: PKGPT vs. human expert — physiological plausibility failure
numerical_findings.comparison_baseline: Human expert model (13.2 L is physiologically consistent)

numerical_findings.description: Theophylline CL estimate: PKGPT vs. human expert

gaps_addressed: Activity 1 benchmark anchor: first agentic NONMEM system benchmarked against human expert models with quantitative OFV and parameter estimates — the comparative activity can position Claude/Codex/Antigravity against PKGPT's documented gaps (covariate failure, V2 plausibility, reproducibility)

Activity 2 failure mode evidence: V2=149 L vs 13.2 L is a documented real-world plausibility failure (M4.3 category: plausibility error) and covariate identification failure is a structural reasoning gap
Establishes that agentic execution (PKGPT) is categorically different from static zero-shot prompting — relevant to interpreting Codex agent capability
Three public benchmark datasets (warfarin, theophylline, tobramycin) proposed as standard test cases for comparative activities

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search during Activity 1 literature support (PMID 42076151). DOI 10.3390/pharmaceutics18040501 (Pharmaceutics vol 18 issue 4). Open access via PMC13118610. Note: distinct from pkgpt_2026 in library (DOI 10.3390/pharmaceutics18020215, vol 18 issue 2, Chen et al.) — same journal and topic but different groups and different numerical results. This paper provides the only quantitative human-vs-LLM OFV comparison and the tobramycin V2 plausibility failure, which are the key anchor points for Activity 1/2 scoring design.
